newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Cubic unsure will meet estimates.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Cubic unsure will meet estimates.

text.p: Cubic Corp Chief Financial Officer William Boyle on Wednesday said he was "no longer certain" the company would reach fiscal 1997 earnings estimates that he made months ago.

"Some unanticipated factors have led to uncertainty as to whether we can still meet that," Boyle said in an interview. "We may still meet that in the future...but we're no longer comfortable making the projections." In February, he said he expected earnings for the year ending September 30 to rise to $1.35 a share from $1.23 the previous 12 months.

In explaining the uncertainty, Boyle cited a recent decision to speed up a new product introduction, as well as unexpected costs related to a defense contract and a recent British acquisition. Still, he said all three "unanticipated factors" involved activities that pointed to growth in the long term.

Cubic, a 45-year-old company based in San Diego, has two focuses. It creates computerized systems for collecting bus and railway fares, and it makes tactical training equipment for the defense industry.
The company decided Tuesday to spend about $2 million in fiscal 1997 to speed up the introduction of a technology that incorporates sound and video with electronic mail messages, he said.
Boyle said the "enthusiastic response" to a preview of the product at a recent technology conference convinced company officials to push to get it on the market before the Christmas sales season.
The company also recently discovered that it was facing unexpected development costs related to one of its defense contracts, called MILES 2000, with the U.S. army.
